title: Rename workbench cannot save backend-generated regression cases through the strict HTTP contract
observed_behavior: The route contract advertises kind, expected_episode, expected_episode_title, expected_movie_title, expected_year, and template_preset, and the backend preview emits several of them in case_payload. The WebView posts that payload unchanged, but RenameFilterCaseCommandPayload inherits extra=forbid and declares none of those six fields, so HTTP/Pydantic validation rejects the request before the route handler runs. Backend preview may also emit additional filter-option fields that the strict model does not declare.
expected_invariant: Every documented or backend-generated field submitted to an active Local API route must validate against that route's Pydantic request model; a backend-produced save payload must round-trip through the HTTP boundary.
root_cause: The route contract, preview response builder, and strict command payload model evolved independently. Direct handler/facade tests bypass the Pydantic HTTP envelope and therefore did not expose the cross-layer schema drift.
failure_scenario: An operator runs a complete movie or TV rename workbench comparison and selects Save Case. The backend-generated case_payload includes kind and template_preset plus mode-specific expected fields; the WebView submits it to /api/rename/filter-cases, validation returns an extra-forbidden error, and the regression corpus is not updated.
evidence: api_routes_command_operations.py advertises six fields absent from RenameFilterCaseCommandPayload: kind, expected_episode, expected_episode_title, expected_movie_title, expected_year, and template_preset.
A current-tree bundled-Python reproduction validated each advertised field independently and all six returned Pydantic error type extra_forbidden.
_case_payload_for_preview always emits kind and template_preset and emits movie/TV-specific expected fields; it can additionally emit filter-option and remove-term fields.
saveRenameWorkbenchCase copies payload.case_payload and submitRenameBadCasePayload posts that object to /api/rename/filter-cases.
The mapped HTTP handler validates the route-specific Pydantic model before command dispatch.
affected_flows: Rename workbench preview -> backend case_payload -> Save Case -> POST /api/rename/filter-cases
Rename bad-case regression corpus capture and future filter-regression coverage
existing_safeguards: The route uses strict JSON parsing, a route-specific extra=forbid Pydantic model, confirm_append, authenticated loopback access, and backend-owned corpus mutation.
safeguard_gap: The strict model is stale relative to both the public route contract and backend-generated payload, turning a request-integrity safeguard into a deterministic rejection of the supported UI workflow.
tests_present: Rename filter-case handler/facade tests exercise _rename_filter_case_payload directly.
Cross-cutting route-contract and payload-registry tests verify route presence and model registration.
tests_missing: HTTP-level test posting the exact case_payload returned by rename filename preview.
Contract-to-Pydantic field parity test for extra=forbid routes.
WebView/backend round-trip test for movie and TV Save Case workflows.
recommended_remediation: Define one shared regression-case request schema and use it for the route contract, preview case_payload, and RenameFilterCaseCommandPayload. At minimum add all supported emitted fields with appropriate types, reject or deliberately normalize unsupported optional fields, and add an HTTP round-trip test using the exact backend preview payload.
remediation_risk: medium: changes a strict test-fixture-write contract and corpus serialization; validate compatibility and confirmation behavior, but no source-media mutation or real-media run is required
validation_rung: Targeted Pydantic contract tests, strict-JSON Local API route tests, rename preview/save integration tests, affected WebView static/browser smoke, and change-packet coverage.
prior_audit_relationship: No matching defect was found in the scoped prior/current worker finding ledgers; newly observed by the route-to-model-to-frontend join.

title: API route inventory section counts understate POST and process-command rows
observed_behavior: The inventory's total states 172 routes = 55 GET + 117 POST, and a deterministic table-row parser confirms 172 unique rows with exactly 55 GET and 117 POST. However, the POST section heading says 116 routes, and the Process Commands heading says 18 routes although that section contains 19 POST rows.
expected_invariant: Machine- and human-facing inventory counts must agree with the route rows they summarize so audit coverage and change-control scope cannot be understated.
root_cause: Manually maintained section-count labels drifted from the underlying route tables; current route-presence checks do not assert internal heading arithmetic.
failure_scenario: An auditor or maintenance script trusts the section headings and budgets coverage for 116 POST routes or 18 process commands, omitting one active command despite the correct row being present elsewhere in the document.
evidence: Line 7 states 55 GET plus 117 POST for 172 total routes.
A current-tree quote-safe parser counted 172 unique table rows: 55 GET, 117 POST, and 19 rows inside the Process Commands section.
affected_flows: Repository-wide Local API audits and coverage accounting
existing_safeguards: The document contains explicit per-route rows, the top-level total is arithmetically correct, and route inventory tests compare important route content against executable contracts.
safeguard_gap: No check derives section headings from their table rows or rejects stale manual counts.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_api_route_inventory.py validates inventory/contract relationships and route documentation.
tests_missing: Heading-to-table count parity for GET, POST, and each named route group.
Generated count refresh or a lint rule that prevents manual count drift.
recommended_remediation: Correct the two stale headings and add a deterministic inventory lint/test that derives counts from route rows (or generate the headings from the same route source) so future additions cannot leave arithmetic stale.
remediation_risk: low: documentation and inventory-test correction only
validation_rung: Targeted API inventory tests, Markdown route/count parity check, link/path checks if affected, and change-packet validation; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: No matching defect was found in the scoped prior/current worker finding ledgers; newly observed by deterministic inventory-row reconciliation.
